decisions.reason: As a modest extension of the established radiant-heater business with lower visibility and commitment than the flagship lines, it is somewhat easier to withdraw, but in a growing firm and market management would still usually continue it.

Because it is a multi-model flagship line publicly tied to the firm's strategic shift toward broader lower-carbon climate solutions, sunk investment and the need to justify the announced direction strongly favor retaining it.

This product has visible market presence but is not described as strategic, so it is more exposed if results disappoint, yet escalation of commitment and the firm's growth make continued support more likely than a quick withdrawal.

A multi-model industrial electric infrared line fits closely with the firm's existing customer base and direction, so prior development effort and reasonable scope to blame weak early results on temporary market factors support keeping it.

This hydrogen-capable flagship line is highly central to the firm's publicly stated future, with a named launch and real-site reference, making management especially likely to persist despite any early disappointment.
